stimulus.body: A 2005 panel of 450 retirees in West Africa showed 58% followed the expected sequence of education, work, and family, while 30% took a different order.

questions.stem: Explain the 2005 Africa finding about life course.

answer.exemplar: A 2005 panel of 450 retirees in West Africa showed 58% followed the expected sequence of education, work, and family, while 30% took a different order. This illustrates life course: the socially patterned sequence of roles and events across a lifetime. A careful reading links the group-level pattern to the wider social structure rather than to any single person. A complete response names the concept, defines it, and supports the definition with the contrasting shares in the data.

questions.explanation: The finding illustrates life course: the socially patterned sequence of roles and events across a lifetime. The 58 percent versus 30 percent split in West Africa supplies the evidence a full response should cite.
questions.hint: Think about the social force behind the two figures.

stimulus.body: A 2007 panel of 450 retirees in West Africa showed 70% followed the expected sequence of education, work, and family, while 10% took a different order.

questions.stem: What is the point gap in the 2007 Africa life course survey?
questions.explanation: Subtracting 10 percent from 70 percent gives 60 percentage points, the gap reported in the 2007 data from West Africa between the two shares.
questions.hint: Look past the numbers to the relationship they describe.
